note: Proposed synthetic test inputs only. The given observations are hypothetical assumptions, not reconstructions of real incidents. Expected values describe application-layer assessments for a possible future integration; they are not core VAP/CAP verifier verdicts, registered schema events, executed-test results, or findings of legal compliance. Structural validation of this catalogue does not execute its cases. No absence of evidence establishes absence of activity outside the declared observation scope.

cases.title: Unapproved destination is denied within an observed route
given: An application routes its upload requests through a configured policy-enforcement gateway.
The selected destination, unapproved.example.invalid, is absent from the applicable approved-destination registry.
The gateway denies this request before dispatch and records no dispatch for its request identifier.
The evidence covers this gateway route and does not cover all devices, accounts, or alternative network paths.

reasons: The destination is not approved for this request.
No dispatch was observed for this request on the covered route; other routes remain outside the claim.

forbidden_conclusions: No external upload occurred anywhere.
The organization prevented every possible disclosure.
The denial establishes legal compliance.

cases.title: Approved provider with the wrong tenant is denied
given: The registry approves ai.example.invalid only for tenant-enterprise-a and the stated processing purpose.
The proposed request uses the same provider but is authenticated to tenant-personal-b.
The gateway can bind the authenticated tenant and destination to the proposed request.
No exception authorizes tenant-personal-b.

reasons: Provider-level approval does not authorize a different tenant or account.
The requested tenant fails the approval binding before dispatch.

forbidden_conclusions: Any account at an approved provider is approved.
The provider's brand or hostname alone proves an appropriate contractual arrangement.
A matching provider identifier overrides a tenant mismatch.

cases.title: Expired or stale authorization requires review
given: A cached permit refers to policy version policy-v1 and has passed its validity deadline.
The application cannot establish whether policy-v1 is still the currently applicable policy.
The payload and destination match the cached permit.
The gateway has not dispatched the request.

reasons: Matching content and destination do not refresh an expired decision.
A new applicable policy evaluation is needed before the controlled route may proceed.

forbidden_conclusions: A historically permitted request remains permitted indefinitely.
An expired permit is valid because its signature still verifies.
Review status itself authorizes dispatch.

cases.title: Payload substitution after authorization is denied
given: A permit binds the exact outgoing payload digest, destination, tenant, purpose, and policy version.
After the permit is issued, the outgoing payload bytes change.
The gateway computes the digest of the actual outgoing bytes and finds a mismatch.
The request has not yet been dispatched.

reasons: The permit does not cover the bytes now proposed for transfer.
A replacement payload needs a new policy evaluation and binding.

forbidden_conclusions: An unchanged filename establishes an unchanged payload.
The old permit authorizes every revision of the file.
An intact permit signature proves that the outgoing content was authorized.

cases.title: Observed transmission after denial is a control violation
given: The applicable policy decision denies a request identified by request-005.
A separately authenticated egress observation binds a transmission to request-005, the same payload, destination, and tenant.
The observation falls within the declared monitoring scope and relevant time interval.
No authorized override or later permit covers the observed transmission.

reasons: The observed action conflicts with the bound denial.
The denial record cannot substitute for evidence that the enforcement control actually stopped the request.

forbidden_conclusions: The upload was prevented because a denial was logged.
The valid signatures make the action policy-compliant.
This application-layer violation is already a final legal finding.

cases.title: Timeout after dispatch leaves remote outcome unknown
given: The gateway records dispatch of an authorized request to ai.example.invalid.
The connection times out before a usable destination acknowledgement is received.
The available evidence does not establish whether the provider accepted or processed the request.
The integration has not established a provider-supported idempotency or reconciliation guarantee for this operation.

reasons: A timeout does not distinguish rejection from acceptance followed by a lost response.
Blind repetition could duplicate a transfer or processing action.

forbidden_conclusions: The provider received no data.
The provider definitely completed processing.
Retrying the request is necessarily harmless.

cases.title: A possible bypass outside coverage remains unknown
given: The collector observes only the managed application's API route.
An alternative browser or unmanaged device can reach external services outside that route.
No upload record appears in the managed application's collected records for the relevant interval.
No additional evidence resolves whether a transfer occurred through the uncovered path.

reasons: The available observations cannot resolve activity on an uncovered path.
The absence of an application event supports only the narrower statement that this collector did not observe one.

forbidden_conclusions: No AI service was used.
An uncovered upload definitely occurred.
The managed route's record completeness establishes organization-wide completeness.

cases.title: Unavailable collector blocks only the controlled application route
given: The application's configured policy requires a functioning evidence collector before this class of upload may be dispatched.
The collector is unavailable and cannot acknowledge durable collection.
The gateway can hold requests on its own route before transmission.
The application does not control every other device, network path, or AI client.

reasons: This application's configured prerequisite for dispatch is unsatisfied.
Blocking the covered route says nothing conclusive about activity elsewhere.

forbidden_conclusions: VAP itself stopped all network transfers.
No information left the organization while the collector was down.
Collector unavailability is a core VAP/CAP verifier verdict.

cases.title: A deletion request establishes a request only
given: An authenticated local record contains a deletion request for object-synthetic-001 in tenant-enterprise-a.
The request identifies the intended provider and the requested scope.
No destination acknowledgement, provider deletion statement, or independent review is available.

reasons: The available record establishes the recorded request and its declared scope.
It does not establish receipt or action by the provider.

forbidden_conclusions: The object has been erased.
The provider received or accepted the request.
The request proves deletion from backups or training data.

cases.title: An acknowledgement does not establish completed deletion
given: The provider authenticates a response acknowledging receipt of a bound deletion request.
The acknowledgement identifies the matching tenant, object set, and request identifier.
The response says the request is queued and contains no completion claim.
No subsequent completion evidence is available.

reasons: Receipt of a queued request is established within the stated assumptions.
Acknowledgement and completion are distinct events.

forbidden_conclusions: A successful acknowledgement means deletion completed.
A queued request proves that all copies are inaccessible.
Receipt of the request discharges all applicable legal obligations.

cases.title: A signed deletion attestation excluding backups remains scoped
given: A provider statement is signed by the expected provider identity and binds the correct request, tenant, and object set.
The statement claims removal from active serving storage at a specified time.
The statement expressly excludes backups and does not address model-training use or derivative material.
No independent assessment of the provider's deletion process is available.

reasons: The signature attributes a defined claim to the provider; it does not independently establish the truth of every claimed action.
Backups, training use, and derivative material are outside the supported claim.

forbidden_conclusions: All copies were universally erased.
A valid signature is independent proof of physical deletion.
The attestation proves removal from model weights or every derivative.

cases.title: A mismatched deletion receipt cannot support the target claim
given: The target deletion request concerns object-synthetic-004 in tenant-enterprise-a.
A cryptographically authentic provider receipt instead binds object-synthetic-elsewhere in tenant-enterprise-b.
No documented object mapping, tenant migration, or corrected receipt connects the receipt to the target request.
No other completion evidence is available for the target object.

reasons: An authentic receipt for a different scope does not support this deletion claim.
The target request remains unresolved without matching evidence.

forbidden_conclusions: Any receipt from the provider proves the requested deletion.
Valid signature verification cures mismatched scope.
The mismatch proves that the target object was retained.

cases.title: Independent review supports only the reviewed deletion scope
given: An independent reviewer documents a method, evidence set, observation interval, and limitations for a deletion review.
The reviewed scope covers the named synthetic objects in specified active-storage locations of tenant-enterprise-a.
The reviewer reports completion within that scope and binds the report to the relevant request and object set.
Backups, unobserved replicas, downstream recipients, and model-training derivatives are expressly excluded.

reasons: The independent report adds evidence only for the objects, locations, time, and method it actually covers.
The report's exclusions and limitations remain part of the assessment.

forbidden_conclusions: Independent review proves universal irreversible erasure.
Excluded locations or derivatives were also verified.
A limited technical review is a legal compliance determination.

cases.title: Authentic evidence and disclosure do not override an AI-use prohibition
given: The publication's applicable policy version prohibits the recorded type of AI use at the current submission stage.
Integrity and identity checks for the evidence records have succeeded under the stated verification assumptions.
The records bind the prohibited AI use to the exact proposed document revision.
The author has prepared a truthful disclosure of that use and no applicable exception is established.

reasons: Authentic evidence can establish a conflict with the applicable publication policy.
Disclosure does not convert a prohibited activity into a permitted one.

forbidden_conclusions: Integrity verification means the publication is permitted.
Any AI use is acceptable once disclosed.
The application assessment is a legal or institutional adjudication.

cases.title: No AI event with incomplete coverage cannot establish human-only authorship
given: The collected records contain no AI-use event for the proposed document revision.
The collector covers one editor but does not cover external services, imported text, or all collaborator activity.
No independently supported complete provenance claim is available.
The application is asked to classify whether the document involved AI assistance.

reasons: The absence of a collected event does not resolve activity outside the collector's scope.
Human-only authorship is not established by the available evidence.

forbidden_conclusions: The document was created entirely by humans.
AI assistance definitely occurred.
Missing provenance is itself proof of misconduct.

cases.title: An approved document revision changes before submission
given: An editorial approval and disclosure assessment bind document revision revision-a and its exact content digest.
The proposed submission contains revision-b with different content bytes.
No approval or disclosure reassessment binds revision-b.
The workflow requires an approval covering the submitted revision.

reasons: The existing approval covers revision-a rather than the changed submission.
The application must assess the new revision and preserve the earlier revision's evidence.

forbidden_conclusions: An approval automatically covers all future edits.
The same title or filename proves approval applicability.
Revision-b is necessarily prohibited merely because reassessment is pending.

cases.title: Disclosure omits AI involvement in figures or code
given: The applicable policy requires disclosure of AI assistance in text, figures, and code submitted with the work.
Bound evidence records AI assistance for a figure and a code artifact included in the proposed submission.
The prepared disclosure addresses prose editing only and omits those artifacts.
The omission has not been resolved by a documented exception.

reasons: The disclosure does not cover the artifact types required by the applicable policy.
The evidence must bind the figure and code versions as well as the prose revision.

forbidden_conclusions: A prose-only declaration covers every submission component.
AI involvement in an included figure or code artifact is irrelevant by default.
Incomplete disclosure establishes the author's intent.

cases.title: Ambiguous stage-dependent rules require review with stage evidence retained
given: The available policies describe different AI-use rules for drafting, submission, and final publication.
The proposed transition is a revised submission whose governing stage or policy precedence is not resolved by the available policy records.
The evidence identifies AI use during drafting and later edits, with distinct artifact revisions and timestamps.
No authorized interpretation resolves which rule controls the proposed transition.

reasons: The application cannot choose a permissive interpretation without resolving stage and policy applicability.
Earlier activity and the policies applicable to it remain relevant evidence even after the workflow advances.

forbidden_conclusions: A rule permitting AI during drafting necessarily permits it at every later stage.
The newest policy automatically governs every historical action.
Advancing stages removes the need to preserve earlier policy and artifact bindings.

cases.title: A signed self-declaration remains distinct from observed activity
given: An author signs a declaration describing the AI assistance used for a bound document revision.
Signature and identity checks attribute the declaration to that author under the stated assumptions.
No contemporaneous tool observations or independent corroboration establish the declaration's factual completeness.
The available evidence contains no established contradiction of the declaration.

reasons: The signature establishes attribution and integrity of the declaration under the given assumptions.
It does not transform the declaration into directly observed or independently verified activity.

forbidden_conclusions: The signature proves that every factual assertion is true and complete.
The declaration is false because independent observations are unavailable.
Self-declared activity and instrumented observations have identical evidence strength.

cases.title: Prepared or dispatched disclosure has no confirmed receipt or acceptance
given: A disclosure text is prepared and binds the intended document revision, publication destination, and policy version.
The local application records a dispatch attempt to submissions.example.invalid.
No trustworthy destination receipt confirms which disclosure and document revision arrived.
No publisher acknowledgement or editorial acceptance is available.

reasons: Preparation and a local send record do not establish what the publication destination received.
Receipt, if later established, would still be distinct from editorial acceptance or satisfaction of disclosure requirements.

forbidden_conclusions: The disclosure was definitely delivered.
The publisher accepted the submission or approved the AI use.
Preparing or sending a disclosure automatically satisfies the applicable policy or law.
